current_law_statement: Reviewed NRS ch. 239 as published by the Legislative Counsel Bureau (leg.state.nv.us, rev. 4/15/2026, incorporating the 82nd (2023) and 83rd (2025) Sessions and the 2025 36th Special Session) and NAC ch. 239 (rev. 4/13/2026). The fee provisions are stable: NRS 239.052 was last amended in 2013; NRS 239.005(1) ('actual cost') was rewritten and NRS 239.055 (extraordinary-use personnel fee) repealed by S.B. 287 (2019); no 2023-2026 session law amended NRS 239.052-239.054, 239.005 or 239.0107's fee-relevant text. A.B. 51 (2025, Nevada League of Cities), which would have let any governmental entity charge 'a reasonable fee for the use of its personnel or technological resources' under a written policy with advance written notice, died in committee (no further action allowed 2025-04-12). Nevada runs two regimes: (1) statute (NRS 239.052-239.054) binds all 'governmental entities' incl. political subdivisions - copy fees capped at actual direct cost, labor non-chargeable, discretionary waiver by posted written policy, entity-maintained fee list; (2) NAC 239.860-239.869 and the State Library's 2020 manual (adopted by reference) add estimate ($25), deposit (<= estimate), pay-before-receipt and 30-day unclaimed-copy rules for Executive Department agencies ONLY. No AG-issued municipal fee schedule or public-records manual exists; the AG's manuals page lists only OML/rulemaking/boards manuals. Guidance-vs-law gap: the agency manual's overtime carve-out and 'no charge for redaction' statements are guidance, not statute.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (city sets under actual-cost ceiling)
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge. | “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (NRS 239.052 last amended 2013; NRS 239.005(1) amended 2019 SB 287)
resolutions.notes: No statewide per-page figure for municipalities. 'Governmental entity' expressly includes officers and units of a political subdivision (NRS 239.005(5)), so the actual-cost ceiling binds cities. Prior status said 'delegated to regulation'; NRS 239.052(1)'s 'unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee' is an override clause, not a delegation to a municipal fee instrument - no such general instrument exists. NRS 239.052(3) (NV-9006) requires each entity to prepare/maintain and post its own fee list. Direct costs are ink, toner, paper, media, postage. AB 51 (2025), which would have allowed a 'reasonable fee for the use of its personnel or technological resources', died in committee 2025-04-12.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (city sets under actual-cost ceiling)
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge.
resolutions.notes: The prior '50 cents' value belongs to NRS 239.052(4) (law-library copies, NV-0024) - it is NOT a color-copy rate and does not apply to a city's ordinary records. Statute draws no B&W/color distinction; a color copy is capped at its actual direct cost (ink/toner/paper).

resolutions.unit: USD per page/sheet (city sets under actual-cost ceiling)
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge.
resolutions.notes: No oversized/nonstandard rate in statute or regulation. Prior '50 cents' is the law-library ceiling (NRS 239.052(4)), not an oversized rate. Only record-specific overrides: administrative-proceeding transcripts (NRS 239.053, NV-0025) and GIS data (NRS 239.054, NV-0026).

resolutions.unit: USD (city sets under actual-cost ceiling; statutory overrides for transcripts and GIS)
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge. | If a person requests a copy of a transcript of an administrative proceeding that has been transcribed by a certified court reporter, a governmental entity shall charge, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the copy of the transcript is provided, a fee for each page provided which is equal in amount to the fee per page charged by the court reporter for the copy of the transcript, as set forth in the contract between the governmental entity and the court reporter. | A fee for the provision of information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the information is provided, the reasonable costs related to: (a) The gathering and entry of data into the system; (b) Maintenance and updating of the database of the system; (c) Hardware; (d) Software; (e) Quality control; and (f) Consultation with personnel of the governmental entity.
resolutions.notes: Photos/maps: actual direct cost of the medium. Two statutory exceptions to the ceiling: (a) certified-court-reporter transcripts of administrative proceedings - mandatory per-page fee equal to the reporter's contract rate plus medium cost (fixed by contract, NV-0025); (b) GIS information - may include 'reasonable costs' for data gathering/entry, database maintenance, hardware, software, QC and personnel consultation (soft-standard, NV-0026). Prior '50 cents' is law-library only.

resolutions.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.005(1); S.B. 287, 80th Sess. (Nev. 2019) § 13 (repealing NRS 239.055)
resolutions.source_language: “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record. | Sec. 13. NRS 239.055 is hereby repealed.
resolutions.notes: Labor is categorically outside 'actual cost': NRS 239.005(1) excludes any cost 'a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy' (regular staff salaries), and SB 287 (2019) § 13 repealed NRS 239.055, the only authority for an 'extraordinary use of personnel or technology' fee. Applies to cities ('governmental entity' includes political subdivisions). Nuance: the state-agency manual (guidance, Executive Branch only, NV-9007) treats overtime 'actually incurred ... to comply with a request' as chargeable and lists search/retrieval/review/regular staff time as non-chargeable; GIS data (NRS 239.054) alone permits 'reasonable costs' for personnel consultation. AB 51 (2025) would have restored a personnel/technology fee; it died in committee 2025-04-12.

resolutions.source_authority: Nev. Admin. Code § 239.864(1) (Executive Department agencies only); Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.008(3)
resolutions.source_language: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee for providing a copy of a public record: 1. A records official shall provide a person who requests a copy of a public record with an estimate of the fee for the copy, if the estimated actual cost is more than $25. The estimate of the fee must include, without limitation, the amount of postage that the agency will charge the person if the person requested to have the copy delivered by mail.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (NAC 239.864 added R107-13, eff. 12-22-2014; no later amendment)
resolutions.manual_verification: Resolution word per contract rule (agency-only figure -> defers_to_city). Statute is silent for cities; nothing in NRS 239 requires a municipality to issue an estimate at any threshold.
resolutions.notes: State-agency regime: a records official of an agency of the Executive Department shall give a written estimate when estimated actual cost exceeds $25 (NAC 239.864(1); NAC 239.863(1)(f)(2) mirrors it on the request form). NAC 239.860-.869 are adopted under NRS 239.008(3), which reaches only 'an agency of the Executive Department' - they do not bind cities, counties or school districts. Municipal regime: no estimate threshold; a city adopting one may look to the $25 agency figure as guidance.

resolutions.source_language: 2. A records official: (a) May require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay a deposit of not more than the estimate of the actual cost of providing the copy; | If an estimate of the fee exceeds $25, the agency may request a deposit from the person requesting a copy of the record. The agency must provide the person with written notice of the estimated amount of the fee. In such instances, the agency is not required to fulfill the public records request until the person makes a deposit in an amount of the estimated fee.
resolutions.manual_verification: Agency regulation permits a deposit with no dollar threshold; the $25 trigger appears only in the adopted-by-reference manual ('If an estimate of the fee exceeds $25, the agency may request a deposit'). Municipal regime is silent - resolution word follows contract rule for agency-only figures.
resolutions.notes: NRS 239 neither authorizes nor prohibits a municipal deposit/prepayment before search for ordinary copies (existing NV-0018 note). NRS 239.030 makes payment or tender a precondition for CERTIFIED copies (all officers). Agency regime: deposit 'of not more than the estimate' may be required (NAC 239.864(2)(a)); manual ties it to estimates over $25 and says the agency 'is not required to fulfill the public records request until the person makes a deposit'.

resolutions.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.030; Nev. Admin. Code § 239.864(2)(b) (agencies)
resolutions.source_language: Every officer having custody of public records, the contents of which are not declared by law to be confidential, shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying. | (b) Shall require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay the fee for providing the copy, including, without limitation, postage for mailing the copy, if applicable, before the person receives the copy.
resolutions.notes: Statute conditions only CERTIFIED copies on payment/tender of the prescribed fees (NRS 239.030, applies to 'every officer having custody', incl. municipal). For ordinary copies NRS 239 is silent for municipalities - neither authorizes nor bars pay-before-release; the manual (agency guidance) says an agency 'may request payment of the fees prior to releasing the records'. Agency regulation: records official SHALL require payment (incl. postage) before the person receives the copy (NAC 239.864(2)(b)).

resolutions.unit: days after copy reproduced (unclaimed copy may be disposed of)
resolutions.source_authority: Nev. Admin. Code § 239.868(2) (Executive Department agencies only)
resolutions.source_language: If a person who requests to receive a copy of a public record does not claim the copy, the records official may dispose of the copy if the person does not: (a) Claim the copy from the agency; or (b) Notify the agency of when the person will claim the copy, within 30 days after the copy is reproduced.
resolutions.manual_verification: The agency rule addresses unclaimed copies (30 days after reproduction), which is the nearest analogue to a nonpayment consequence; municipal regime silent -> defers_to_city per contract rule. No prior-debt prepayment rule anywhere.
resolutions.notes: No withdrawal-after-N-days or prior-debt provision for any body. Agency regime: unclaimed copies may be disposed of if not claimed (or a pickup date notified) within 30 days after reproduction.

resolutions.notes: No 'no charge below $X' rule. Prior linkage to NV-0022/NV-0027 (statutory free-copy categories) is category-based, not a dollar de-minimis. Waiver of 'all or a portion' of a fee is available by written policy (NRS 239.052(2), NV-0023) - a city could adopt a de-minimis by policy.

resolutions.notes: No minimum fee. A flat minimum would have to be reconciled with the actual-cost ceiling (NRS 239.052(1)).

resolutions.unit: USD per medium (city sets under actual-cost ceiling)
resolutions.source_language: “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
resolutions.notes: 'Media' is expressly a direct cost (NRS 239.005(1)); the entity shall provide an electronic copy by electronic medium if requested (NRS 239.010(4)) and may not refuse a requested medium (239.010(5)(a)). Manual (agencies) lists 'CDs, DVDs, flash (thumb) drives, audiotapes, microfilm' as chargeable media. GIS data may add reasonable system costs (NRS 239.054, NV-0026). Prior linkage to NV-0026 (GIS) was too narrow.

resolutions.source_language: “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
resolutions.notes: 'Postage' is expressly a direct cost. No handling charge (staff time excluded). E-mail delivery has no direct cost. Agency regime: estimate must include postage and payment incl. postage is due before receipt (NAC 239.864). Prior linkage to NV-0026 (GIS) was too narrow.

resolutions.source_language: Every officer having custody of public records, the contents of which are not declared by law to be confidential, shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying.
resolutions.manual_verification: 'such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying' names no prescriber. Searched NRS 239, 266 (general-law cities), 268 (city powers), NAC 239 and the manual for a statewide municipal certification figure - none found; county clerk/recorder fee statutes (NRS ch. 19, 247) are not municipal. For a city the prescribing instrument is its own charter/ordinance fee schedule (and NRS 239.052(3) fee list). Verify agent may prefer delegated_unresolved.
resolutions.notes: Certified copies must be furnished to any person who pays or tenders the prescribed copying and certifying fees. No statewide dollar figure for cities; the copy component remains subject to the actual-cost ceiling of NRS 239.052(1) unless a specific statute sets a fee.

resolutions.unit: USD per recording (medium cost); no per-minute or free-minute figure
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge. | “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
resolutions.notes: Audio/video copies are capped at the actual direct cost of the medium; redaction/staff time not chargeable (see labor items). Prior '50 cents' is the law-library ceiling, not an A/V rate. Body-worn camera records (NRS 289.830(2), applies to city police/marshals) may be 'Requested only on a per incident basis' and inspected on-site only if unredactable confidential content - a request-shape rule, no fee figure. Later-pass: LVMPD v. Center for Investigative Reporting (Nev. 2020) on bodycam redaction fees under the since-repealed NRS 239.055 - not opened in this pass.

resolutions.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. ch. 239 (no commercial-purpose provision)
resolutions.source_language: Searched: NRS ch. 239 (leg.state.nv.us, rev. 4/15/2026, through the 2025 83rd Session and 36th Special Session) incl. NRS 239.005, 239.008, 239.010, 239.0107, 239.011, 239.020, 239.030, 239.052-239.054; NAC ch. 239 (rev. 4/13/2026) incl. NAC 239.860-239.869; SB 287 (2019) enrolled; the State Library's 'Nevada Public Records Act: A Manual for Executive Branch Agencies' (2020, adopted by reference NAC 239.869); AG opinion index hits (AGO 2009-06, AGO 2002-32 - both pre-repeal of NRS 239.055); NRS 266/268 (cities) for a copy/certification fee figure; NRS 289.830 (body-camera records); AB 51 (2025, died in committee 2025-04-12).
resolutions.notes: NRS 239 makes no purpose distinction; 'any person' may inspect/copy (NRS 239.010(1)) and no purpose statement is required. No commercial surcharge and labor cannot become chargeable for commercial requesters (actual-cost ceiling applies to all).

resolutions.value: discretionary; grounds unspecified; requires adopted written policy + posted sign; no purpose statement, written-denial or appeal requirement
resolutions.source_language: A governmental entity may waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record if the governmental entity: (a) Adopts a written policy to waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record; and (b) Posts, in a conspicuous place at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records, a legible sign or notice that states the terms of the policy.
resolutions.notes: Waiver of all or part of a fee is discretionary and conditioned on (a) an adopted written policy and (b) a posted legible sign/notice stating its terms at each office. Statute names no grounds (indigence, public interest, media), no purpose statement, no written denial and no waiver appeal. Mandatory no-fee categories are separate: any specific statute/regulation requiring a free copy (NRS 239.052(1), NV-0022), e.g., VA-eligibility certified copies (NRS 239.020, NV-0027). Manual (agencies): 'All fees waivers must be standardized by a written policy and evenly applied.'

resolutions.notes: No provision that a late response (past the 5th business day, NRS 239.0107) forfeits the copy fee. Remedies for delay are judicial (NRS 239.011: order, costs/attorney fees; NRS 239.012 immunity), not fee forfeiture. Prior linkage to NV-0023/NV-0027 was a mis-tag.

resolutions.notes: No aggregation threshold or carry-forward rule for repeat requests. Agency guidance (manual 2020, NV-9007) bars 'Recouping the original cost of developing or producing the records, in the case of multiple requesters asking for the same records'. NRS 289.830(2)(a) limits body-camera requests to a per-incident basis (police agencies incl. city police).

new_rules.legal_concept: Repeal of extraordinary-use personnel/technology fee (former NRS 239.055)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may no longer charge an additional fee for extraordinary use of its personnel or technological resources in providing a copy of a public record; NRS 239.055 is repealed.
new_rules.trigger: Any request for a copy requiring staff time or technology use
new_rules.source_language: Sec. 13. NRS 239.055 is hereby repealed. | Section 13 of this bill eliminates the authority of a governmental entity to charge an additional fee for providing a copy of a public record when extraordinary use of personnel or resources is required. (NRS 239.055)
new_rules.source_authority: S.B. 287, 80th Sess. (Nev. 2019), § 13 (repealing NRS 239.055); Legislative Counsel's Digest
new_rules.effective_status: Current (repeal effective 2019; NRS 239.055 absent from NRS ch. 239 rev. 4/15/2026)
new_rules.notes: Read with NRS 239.005(1) as amended by the same act (staff costs 'incurred regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy' are not actual cost). Together they make labor categorically non-chargeable for all governmental entities incl. cities. Pre-2019 authorities (AGO 2002-32, AGO 2009-06) on 'extraordinary staff time' are superseded. AB 51 (2025) sought to restore a 'reasonable fee for the use of its personnel or technological resources' and died in committee 2025-04-12.

new_rules.legal_concept: State-agency written estimate when estimated actual cost exceeds $25
new_rules.atomic_rule: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee, its records official shall provide the requester an estimate of the fee (including postage if mail delivery requested) when the estimated actual cost is more than $25.
new_rules.trigger: Estimated actual cost of copies > $25 and agency charges a fee
new_rules.source_language: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee for providing a copy of a public record: 1. A records official shall provide a person who requests a copy of a public record with an estimate of the fee for the copy, if the estimated actual cost is more than $25. The estimate of the fee must include, without limitation, the amount of postage that the agency will charge the person if the person requested to have the copy delivered by mail.
new_rules.notes: Binds only 'an agency of the Executive Department' (adopted under NRS 239.008(3), NRS 378.255). Not applicable to cities; agency figure recorded as guidance for the municipal item. NAC 239.863(1)(f)(2) repeats the $25 figure on the agency request form.

new_rules.legal_concept: State-agency deposit capped at estimated actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: A records official of an Executive Department agency may require the requester to pay a deposit of not more than the estimate of the actual cost of providing the copy.
new_rules.trigger: Agency charges a fee and has estimated the cost
new_rules.source_language: 2. A records official: (a) May require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay a deposit of not more than the estimate of the actual cost of providing the copy;
new_rules.notes: Agencies only. No dollar threshold in the regulation; the manual (NV-9008) ties the deposit to estimates over $25. No municipal analogue in NRS 239.

new_rules.legal_concept: State-agency payment in full before copy released
new_rules.atomic_rule: A records official of an Executive Department agency shall require the requester to pay the fee for the copy, including postage if applicable, before the person receives the copy.
new_rules.trigger: Agency charges a fee for a copy
new_rules.source_language: (b) Shall require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay the fee for providing the copy, including, without limitation, postage for mailing the copy, if applicable, before the person receives the copy.
new_rules.notes: Agencies only. For all bodies the only statutory gate is NRS 239.030 (certified copies on payment/tender, NV-0018).

new_rules.legal_concept: State-agency disposal of unclaimed copies after 30 days
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a requester does not claim a reproduced copy, or notify the agency when it will be claimed, within 30 days after reproduction, the records official may dispose of the copy.
new_rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from reproduction of the copy (disposal permitted after)
new_rules.source_language: If a person who requests to receive a copy of a public record does not claim the copy, the records official may dispose of the copy if the person does not: (a) Claim the copy from the agency; or (b) Notify the agency of when the person will claim the copy, within 30 days after the copy is reproduced.
new_rules.notes: Agencies only. Nearest analogue to a nonpayment/abandonment consequence; no municipal rule.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fee list maintained and posted at each office
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity shall prepare and maintain a list of the fees it charges at each office where it provides copies, and post a legible sign stating the fee or the location where the fee list may be obtained.
new_rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall prepare and maintain a list of the fees that it charges at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records. A governmental entity shall post, in a conspicuous place at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records, a legible sign or notice which states: (a) The fee that the governmental entity charges to provide a copy of a public record; or (b) The location at which a list of each fee that the governmental entity charges to provide a copy of a public record may be obtained.
new_rules.notes: The city's own fee list is the operative municipal fee instrument in Nevada; the state sets only the actual-cost ceiling. NRS 239.053(2) adds a posting duty for the transcript surcharge.

new_rules.atomic_rule: An Executive Branch agency may charge for photocopying/photographic reproduction, electronic media, postage/delivery, and overtime actually incurred to comply; it may not charge for review to determine responsiveness, search/retrieval (unless a statute allows), regular staff time, a requester's use of a personal device, or recouping development cost across multiple requesters.
new_rules.source_language: An agency can charge for: Costs for photocopying or photographic reproduction; Costs of electronic or other media, such as CDs, DVDs, flash (thumb) drives, audiotapes, microfilm, etc.; Postage, express mail, delivery services, etc.; Overtime, if it is actually incurred by the agency in order to comply with a request. Fees are not a revenue-generating operation of an agency. An agency may not charge a fee for: Review of a record to determine if the record is a responsive record. Searching for or retrieving documents, unless otherwise allowed by statute. Regular staff time for complying with a public records request. Requestor’s use of a personal device to copy or photograph public records. Recouping the original cost of developing or producing the records, in the case of multiple requesters asking for the same records.
new_rules.source_authority: Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, 'Nevada Public Records Act: A Manual for Executive Branch Agencies' (Bulletin No. 3 rev., Aug. 2020), pp. 18-19; adopted by reference NAC 239.869
new_rules.effective_status: Current (2020 edition; NAC 239.869 adopts the 2014 edition and approved subsequent editions)
new_rules.notes: Guidance for Executive Department agencies only, but it is the only official Nevada text spelling out what 'actual cost' excludes; overtime carve-out is guidance, not in statute. Also states an agency 'may not charge the requester for the redaction' before inspection (p. 16). Bullets rendered inline for JSON; verbatim otherwise.

new_rules.legal_concept: State-agency deposit when estimate exceeds $25; no duty to fulfill until deposit paid
new_rules.atomic_rule: If an agency's fee estimate exceeds $25 it may request a deposit, must give written notice of the estimated amount, and is not required to fulfill the request until the deposit (in the amount of the estimated fee) is made.
new_rules.source_language: If an estimate of the fee exceeds $25, the agency may request a deposit from the person requesting a copy of the record. The agency must provide the person with written notice of the estimated amount of the fee. In such instances, the agency is not required to fulfill the public records request until the person makes a deposit in an amount of the estimated fee.
new_rules.source_authority: Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, 'Nevada Public Records Act: A Manual for Executive Branch Agencies' (2020), p. 19 'Fee Deposit'
new_rules.notes: Executive Department agencies only. Manual's response checklist (p. 23) adds: 'If the agency requires prepayment: No further work on the request need be taken until the estimated fees (if applicable) have been deposited' and 'If the estimated fee exceeds $25: The requester must acknowledge and approve the fee in writing before the agency fulfills the request.' No municipal analogue.

repeal confirmed; digest: eliminates authority to charge additional fee for extraordinary use of personnel or resources

applicability_notes: 'Governmental entity' (NRS 239.005(5)) includes officers and units of a political subdivision, so NRS 239.052-239.054, 239.005(1), 239.030 and 239.0107 bind cities directly.

NAC 239.860-239.869 are promulgated under NRS 239.008(3), which reaches only 'an agency of the Executive Department'; every $ figure they carry ($25 estimate threshold, deposit <= estimate, 30-day unclaimed disposal) is agency-only and is recorded as guidance for the municipal item (defers_to_city), never as a municipal value.

The 2020 State Library manual is adopted by reference for Executive Department agencies (NAC 239.869); its overtime carve-out and redaction no-charge statement are not in statute and are not municipal law.
The 50-cents-per-page figure in NRS 239.052(4) is a ceiling for copies from a governmental law library only; it was mis-attached in the prior to color/oversized/specialty/AV items.
NRS 239.053 (transcript surcharge) and NRS 239.054 (GIS reasonable costs) apply to any governmental entity holding such records, incl. cities.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate, color/oversized/specialty rate, page bands, free-page allowance, de-minimis, minimum fee, or certification fee for municipalities - only the actual-cost ceiling.

No estimate threshold, requester response window, revision trigger, estimate validity, deposit threshold or deposit cap for municipalities (all exist only for Executive Department agencies via NAC 239.864 / manual).
No statutory clock effect (tolling/pause) tied to fee estimates or unpaid deposits for any body; NRS 239.0107 is silent.
No commercial-purpose distinction, no fee forfeiture on late response, no repeat-request aggregation or carry-forward rule.
No electronic-payment-method requirement in NRS 239 / NAC 239.
AB 51 (2025) - personnel/technology fee for all governmental entities - failed; labor remains non-chargeable.
gaps_manual_verification: certification: NRS 239.030 'as may be prescribed' resolved defers_to_city; a verifier may prefer delegated_unresolved. No statewide municipal certification-fee instrument found (NRS 239/266/268, NAC 239, manual searched).
labor.programming.rate: creation of new records / data extraction not addressed for municipalities (NAC 239.867 applies to agencies).
payment.method: only NRS 239 / NAC 239 searched; general local-government e-payment authority outside ch. 239 not researched.
rules.deposit.threshold: agency $25 deposit trigger comes from the manual (guidance) not from NAC 239.864(2)(a) which sets no threshold.
Case law not opened: LVMPD v. Center for Investigative Reporting (Nev. 2020) on bodycam redaction fees (decided under repealed NRS 239.055) - later pass if needed.
